metadata.title: Why SpaceX's IPO sets Elon Musk to become the world's first trillionaire

content.text:
SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk was propelled to trillionaire status — the first-ever in history — on Friday as SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO) became the latest addition to his publicly traded corporate empire.
Morning Brief host Julie Hyman is joined by Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Pras Subramanian and Trustless Media Founder Zack Guzman to discuss.
Musk is pretty much guaranteed to become a trillionaire, right? Even at 135, he's a trillionaire because his SpaceX stake is worth $690 billion at that 135. Tesla his net worth there is about $279 billion. So, um, you know, looks like
he's probably going to make it if the if the stock uh gains at all. Obviously, his his growth in profile and wealth has come with um, you know, some criticism, right? That that activists have pushed back against him as a rich person, you know, but also his government involvement last year didn't help matters.
Right. I mean, if you look at the numbers, he's made a tremendous amount of money since Trump was elected, right? That that whole bet has paid off treme big time for him. But yeah, you have the connection with the White House and the administration, but also just a lot of things he's posting on X
is which which which is a story in itself in the fact that he's putting a lot of stuff out that's pretty controversial and and offensive to some people and it doesn't seem to matter.
It doesn't seem to be he's not being punished like a normal CEO would have been punished, right? Like lost his job, company shares going down. It doesn't seem to matter when it comes to SpaceX. Like that's all forgiven, all forgotten.
Well not even just SpaceX, it seems to that the the rules, normal rules in general do not apply to him. I mean, and and that goes back to the fact that he has 85% voting share in SpaceX as well. It goes back to the fact that he put it at 135 and that and he's just like, I declare. It goes back to the fact that all the brokerages are restricting people from um, you know, from retail investors that this is the price of admission that they're not allowed to sell their shares for a while. Like to me, that all comes back to the power of Elon Musk.
I mean, it wasn't too long ago when you think about kind of when Tesla's shares were under pressure back when he was still kind of doing the doge things. Uh and and that was I guess a little bit different because there was a way, obviously with Tesla, more people buy cars than spaceships. Uh so I think there was a way for the average consumer to maybe fight back or maybe, you know, we saw all the stickers of like, I bought this Tesla before uh Elon was Elon. Uh and so like there is a little bit of a difference, I think with this one specifically just because
of it being a more of a B2B than a B2C play. But I think, you know, a lot of people thought that that was a terrible move back then. And now, I guess, you know, this is one of those clear cases of someone in this camp, a very rich man, makes the bet and now it's playing out and to your point, Julie, getting to change all the rules and I don't know how many of those rules would be able to be changed if he didn't kind of align himself.
